thought: plain iron, the sort Horvik sells over the counter; jab at off-the-peg kit
line: Straight off Horvik's counter, that iron? Still smells of the shop.

thought: iron and a green look; new lot come up the road from Lumbridge
line: Fresh up from Lumbridge, that one, and clanking like a pail.

thought: anyone can wear iron and Horvik sells it to anyone; gripe at Horvik
line: Horvik sells iron to anyone with a purse. No standards, that man.

thought: grey plate from a distance looks official; corrects herself
line: Here, is that a guard? No... just somebody in iron.

thought: iron is weak; the dark wizards on the Lumbridge road won't be bothered
line: Iron armour! The dark wizards will be ever so worried.

thought: dark grey metal on an overcast day
line: Grey armour on a grey morning. Well, it matches.

thought: iron is only a step above bronze
line: A step up from bronze, iron is. A small step, mind.

thought: Horvik has steel too, why stop at iron
line: Did nobody tell you Horvik does steel as well, guv?

thought: heard anyone can wear iron without training; looks like it
line: Anyone can wear iron, they say. Looks like anyone has.

thought: the clank of plate going up the street, like a tinker's cart
line: Clank, clank, all the way up the road. Like a tinker's cart.

thought: iron is what you'd wear to fight goblins
line: Dressed for the goblins, is it? They'll be quaking.

thought: iron is a stage on the way to steel; mock sympathy to a neighbour
line: Don't laugh. Somebody's saving up for steel, I expect.

thought: dull grey iron moving about looks like a coal scuttle
line: Coal scuttle on legs... and it's coming this way.

thought: the muggers go after money; iron says no money
line: The muggers won't look twice at iron. That's one blessing.

thought: her own kettle is dull, but the iron is duller
line: And I thought my old kettle was dull. Look at that iron.

thought: steel with a fresh shine; someone's cleaned it this morning
line: That steel's had a rag over it this morning, I can tell.

thought: steel is brighter than iron and catches the light
line: Brighter than iron, steel. Catches the light in the square.

thought: smart steel; measured by the guards at the gates
line: You'd not look out of place on the city gate in that.

thought: values not being overcharged; steel from Horvik is a fair buy
line: Steel's a good honest buy. Horvik won't have robbed you on that.

thought: noticed the upgrade from iron
line: Ooh, steel. Somebody's moved on from iron.

thought: heard steel takes coal as well as iron; worth the trouble
line: Takes coal as well as iron to make steel, they say. Worth it, mind.

thought: points the steel out to a friend
line: Look, that one's in steel. Tidy, isn't it?

thought: the sun is out and steel shows best in it
line: Good day for it. Steel looks its best when the sun's out.

thought: it sits well; some people wear plate like a barrel
line: Sits well on you, that steel. Some folk wear it like a barrel.

thought: she'd have steel herself, if she ever left the square
line: Steel... now that's what I'd have, if I ever left the square.

thought: steel costs some saving; trips to the bank
line: Must have cost a fair few trips to the bank, that steel.

thought: a tidy adventurer, unlike most of them
line: Now that's what a proper adventurer looks like. Steel, see?

thought: nothing flash, and that's a good thing
line: Sensible steel. Nothing flash, and nothing wrong with it.

thought: most adventurers go about in rags; gripe, then praise
line: Half these adventurers go about in rags. Nice to see steel for once.

thought: the shine reminds her of a new kettle
line: Cor, you're bright as a new kettle in that steel!

thought: red armour, nothing like the new lot from Lumbridge
line: Red armour! Not something you see on the Lumbridge road.

thought: measured against Horvik's window; nothing there like it
line: Nothing in Horvik's window comes close to that red armour.

thought: heard it takes a lot of training to wear
line: You need a good deal of training to wear that red, they say.

thought: heard it can't be smithed, only found
line: Word is nobody can smith red metal like that. Has to be found.

thought: tells a neighbour to make room for the red armour
line: Look, red armour. Shift over and let them by.

thought: red is hard to wear well
line: That red suits you. Not everybody can carry it off.

thought: it comes off fierce monsters; guesses at the monster
line: Must have been a rough old monster that gave that up.

thought: a cheerful colour in a grey square
line: Red's a cheerful colour on a grey day in the square.

thought: her own modest saving for a hat
line: All that red metal... and I've been saving for a new hat since spring.

thought: recognises the red metal
line: Is that dragon metal? Well I never.

thought: looks hard, good between a body and trouble
line: Looks hard as anything, that red. Good between you and trouble.

thought: most folk round here couldn't tell good metal; she can
line: Half the folk round here couldn't tell dragon metal from rust. I can.

thought: plain delight at the real thing
line: Ooh, that's proper dragon armour, that is!

thought: nudges a friend: that one's done well
line: That one's done well for themselves. Red armour, see?

thought: the red makes the plain guards look drab by comparison
line: Makes the guards look like pigeons, red armour like that.

thought: red plate to walk past the tea stall; too much
line: Red armour to walk past a tea stall? Bit much, that.

thought: the thieves would see that red from the gate
line: All that red, and the pickpockets have spotted you from the gate.

thought: red as a cooked lobster
line: Red as a cooked lobster. Fresh out of the pot, are we?

thought: it can't be smithed, so you can't order it in a quieter colour
line: Can't be smithed, that red. So no asking for it in brown.

thought: points out someone dressed like a tomato
line: Here, someone's gone and dressed as a tomato.

thought: the ones in red always stand in the middle of the square
line: Always the ones in red armour stood in the middle of the square.

thought: it fetches a high price, and the colour comes with it
line: Must have cost a fortune. Shame the colour came with it.

thought: red is not a quiet colour
line: Hope you weren't trying to be quiet, in that red.

thought: her house is worth less than one piece of it
line: My whole house wouldn't buy one boot of that red.

thought: warm day for plate; you'll cook
line: Warm day for plate. You'll be cooked in that red by noon.

thought: the guards will think it's a parade
line: Through the gate in that red? The guards will think it's a parade.

thought: everyone is looking at the red one
line: That one wants looking at, and in that red, everyone is.

thought: their money, but that much red in this town
line: Well, it's your money. But that much red, in this town?

thought: all that training and nobody mentioned the colour
line: Years of training to wear it, and nobody mentioned the colour?

thought: a flash of red looked like a fire on a roof
line: Thought a roof was on fire. It's only that red armour.

thought: heard only well-trained fighters can use one
line: Only a well-trained fighter can handle a whip like that, they say.

thought: values a fair price; the whip is strong and not dear
line: Sensible buy, a whip. Strong, and doesn't cost the earth.

thought: it came off a demon, so it was earned
line: Off a demon, that whip. You'll have earned it, then.

thought: recognises the whip; every serious fighter has one
line: Ooh, a whip! Every serious fighter has one, they say.

thought: warns a neighbour a real fighter is coming
line: Mind out, there's a fighter coming. See the whip?

thought: she moves for nobody, but would for that whip
line: I'd move for that whip, and I don't move for anyone.

thought: plenty of whips pass; this one's well kept
line: Plenty of whips come through here. Yours is kept nice.

thought: she'd like one for the pigeons on her sill
line: I could do with a whip like that for the pigeons on my sill.

thought: the look of it says the Abyss
line: Is that from the Abyss? It's got that look about it.

thought: neat kit, and quick, she hears
line: Neat bit of kit, that whip. Quick as anything, I hear.

thought: red and black with a barbed point; not one to argue with
line: Red and black, and barbed at the end. Wouldn't want to argue with it.

thought: swords catch on the stalls; a whip is tidier
line: Swords catch on every stall in this square. A whip's much tidier.

thought: took it for a rope, then saw it properly
line: That's a rope... no, a whip. A proper one, too.

thought: the city guards would be better off with whips like that
line: The guards on the gate could do with a few of those whips.

thought: a whip needs a quick wrist; the player looks it
line: Takes a quick wrist, a whip. You look like you've got one.

thought: a whip in town; herding chickens
line: A whip in the square. Planning to herd the chickens, are we?

thought: everyone has one; there must be a queue at the Abyss
line: Another whip. There must be a queue of you at the Abyss.

thought: it came off a demon; wants a scrub
line: Off a demon, that whip? It wants a good scrub, then.

thought: they all carry whips; all the same
line: Look, another one with a whip. All the same, that lot.

thought: whips everywhere, like a cattle market
line: Whips on every corner. Like a cattle market, this town.

thought: a whip and no horse
line: Does it come with a horse, that whip?

thought: the segmented lash looks like something the sewer rats would drag
line: Looks like something the sewer rats would drag about, that.

thought: the old warning about losing an eye
line: You'll have someone's eye out with that, mark my words.

thought: she never trusts a weapon that bends
line: Never trust a weapon that bends, I always say.

thought: fighting or keeping goats in line
line: Is that for fighting, or for keeping goats in line?

thought: heard every serious fighter has one; so every fighter has one
line: Everyone serious has a whip, they say. So everyone has one.

thought: the whip swung near her clean coat
line: Watch it! I've only just had this coat cleaned.

thought: tells a friend not to stand behind the whip
line: Don't stand behind that one. The whip comes back, mind.

thought: the demon that dropped it probably wasn't sorry
line: A demon dropped that, and I'd say it wasn't sorry to see it go.

thought: whips are for carters
line: Fancy yourself a carter, do you, with that whip?

thought: the blue-green runite catches her eye
line: Ooh, runite! That colour always catches the eye.

thought: heard it takes a master smith, near enough
line: Takes a master smith to forge a rune scimitar, near enough.

thought: the swordshop only does daggers and plain swords
line: You'll not find that scimitar in the swordshop. Daggers, mostly.

thought: the curve of the blade says someone knows what they're doing
line: Look at the curve on that sword. Someone knows their business.

thought: second only to the red ones, she hears
line: Very smart blade. Second only to the red ones, I hear.

thought: either a fire giant or a dear smith
line: Must have taken a fire giant down for that, or paid a smith dearly.

thought: fire giants drop them; she'd not go near one
line: Fire giants drop those, so I hear. You'd not catch me near one.

thought: not many walk the square with rune
line: Not many walk through the square with rune. You'll turn heads.

thought: it looks at home in the hand
line: Had that scimitar long? It looks right in your hand.

thought: a curved sword suits someone quick
line: A curved sword like that suits someone quick on their feet.

thought: nothing but rusty daggers round here
line: All rusty daggers round here. Nice to see a proper blade for once.

thought: the edge on it; mind her sleeve
line: Cor, there's an edge on that! Mind my sleeve.

thought: points out the rune scimitar, takes some doing
line: Rune scimitar, see? Takes a bit of doing, that.

thought: prettier than Thessalia's window
line: That blade's prettier than anything in Thessalia's window.

thought: compares it to her own bread knife
line: A rune scimitar... and here's me with a bread knife.

thought: heard it's the best scimitar there is
line: That red scimitar's the best there is, they say.

thought: jagged edge; keep it off her basket
line: Jagged edge on that. Keep it off my basket.

thought: can't be smithed, so somebody had to part with it
line: Can't be smithed, that red blade. Somebody had to part with it.

thought: tells a neighbour to stand aside for the red sword
line: Red sword, look. Stand aside, let it through.

thought: swords like that go through on the way to the Wilderness
line: Swords like that come through here most days, off up north.

thought: red blade reminds her of the beetroot she needs
line: Red blade... that reminds me, I've the beetroot to fetch.

thought: wonders if the red is painted
line: Is that blade painted, or does it come red?

thought: sharper than the swordshop's stock
line: Looks sharper than anything in the swordshop, that.

thought: the gate guards let anything in
line: The guards on the gate let anything through. Red swords and all.

thought: points out the sword nobody can smith
line: Here, that's the sword they say nobody can smith.

thought: wonders if it's heavy
line: Heavy, is it, a sword like that? Looks it.

thought: off north with it; mind the Wilderness
line: Off out north with that, are you? Mind the Wilderness.

thought: a lot of sword for a trip to the bank
line: That's a lot of sword for a trip to the bank.

thought: took the red for blood, then saw it's the colour
line: Blood on the blade... no, it's just the colour of it.

thought: dark hilt, red blade; made to be noticed
line: Dark hilt, red blade. Whoever made that wanted it noticed.

thought: all that green; a cabbage that's been in a fight
line: You look like a cabbage that's been in a fight.

thought: real dragon hide; the dragon may want it back
line: Green dragon, that hide. Hope the dragon didn't want it back.

thought: archer's leathers in the square; pigeons
line: Archer's leathers in the square. Shooting the pigeons, are we?

thought: warns a friend the hide's been out in the Wilderness
line: Don't stand too close. That hide's been out in the Wilderness.

thought: everyone back from the Wilderness smells of dragon
line: Everyone back from the Wilderness smells of dragon. Every one.

thought: leather on a warm day; looks boiled
line: Must be warm, all that green leather. You look a bit boiled.

thought: green like the goblins
line: In green like that, the goblins will take you for family.

thought: she's seen that green coat twice today already
line: I'm sure I've seen that green coat twice today already.

thought: it looks home-made; skinned it yourself
line: Skinned it yourself, did you? It looks home-made.

thought: heard the green dragon hunters get set upon; she can see why
line: Hunters of those green dragons get set upon, they say. I can see why.

thought: very green; hiding in a hedge
line: Very green. Hiding in a hedge later, are we?

thought: scaly green; dressed like a lizard
line: Look at that one, dressed up like a lizard.

thought: mistook it for a dragon, then saw someone in its skin
line: Is that a dragon? No, just somebody wearing its skin.

thought: leather in this weather; sweat like a cheese
line: Funny weather for leather. You'll sweat like a cheese in that.

thought: Thessalia sells robes; less bother than a dragon
line: Thessalia would've sold you a nice robe for half the bother.

thought: heard you can't buy them; earned on the rooftops
line: Can't buy those clothes, they say. Earned on the rooftops, all of it.

thought: the light clothes help a runner get their breath back
line: You'll get your breath back quick in those, I expect.

thought: neat outfit, nothing wasted
line: Very neat, that outfit. Not a wasted stitch on it.

thought: points out a rooftop runner, quick as a cat
line: That's one of the rooftop runners. Quick as a cat, they are.

thought: someone went over the roofs this morning; was it you
line: Somebody went over the roofs this morning. That was you, wasn't it?

thought: light clothes; her coat weighs more than she does
line: Light as a feather, those. My coat weighs more than I do.

thought: moves quietly; she calls that polite
line: You move very quietly in that. Polite, I call it.

thought: passed so fast she nearly lost her basket
line: Ooh, you were quick! Nearly had my basket over.

thought: looks comfortable, better than plate on a warm day
line: Looks comfortable, that. Better than plate on a warm day.

thought: wishes the plate-wearers were as quiet
line: Wish the ones in plate moved as quietly as you.

thought: marks of grace; worked hard for those
line: Marks of grace, is it? You've worked hard for those, then.

thought: so quick they'd be to Lumbridge and back before her kettle boils
line: You'd be to Lumbridge and back before my kettle boiled.

thought: quicker than the pickpockets
line: Mind, that one's quicker than the pickpockets.

thought: someone passed and was gone before she turned
line: Who was that? Oh, they've gone already.

thought: she has no legs for running; tea cold by the time she's home
line: Wish I had the legs for running. My tea's cold before I get home.

thought: someone on her roof at dawn; must have been them
line: That you on my roof at dawn? Thought so.

thought: light clothes look like nightclothes
line: Running about in your nightclothes, are we?

thought: heard they can't be bought with coin; a mercy
line: Can't buy them with coin, they say. Well, there's a mercy.

thought: the rooftop lot are coming; hold your hat
line: Here comes the rooftop lot. Mind the chimney pots.

thought: folk running over roofs; the thatch suffers
line: Folk running over roofs all day. The thatch never stands a chance.

thought: so light a wind would knock you over
line: A strong wind would have you over in that, I should think.

thought: some of us use the road like ordinary people
line: Some of us use the road, like ordinary people.

thought: never walks anywhere, all roofs
line: Do you ever walk anywhere, or is it all roofs?

thought: all that running and still behind at the tea stall
line: All that running, and you're still behind me at the tea stall.

thought: took them for a burglar on the roofs; just a runner
line: Is that a burglar? No, just one of the rooftop runners.

thought: the guards ought to fine rooftop runners for the gutters
line: The guards ought to fine the lot of you for the gutters.

thought: dressed for a race, but strolling
line: All dressed for a race, and strolling. Saving it, are we?

thought: Thessalia would have something smarter
line: Thessalia would have something smarter than that, surely.

thought: she hasn't run since the goblins got in the yard
line: Running clothes. I haven't run since the goblins got in the yard.

thought: light as a moth and as much use in a fight
line: Light as a moth, and about as much use in a fight.

thought: heard the old sets are named for brothers
line: That's one of the brothers' sets, isn't it? Named for them, they say.

thought: old gear, looks like it's seen wars
line: Old gear, that. Looks like it's seen a war or two.

thought: a musty smell of old cellar
line: There's a smell of old cellar off that gear.

thought: tells a friend the old gear wants airing
line: Look at that old gear. Wants a good airing, that does.

thought: six brothers each had a set; imagine the washing
line: Six brothers, they say, and each had a set like that. The washing!

thought: sun's coming out; might dry it out
line: Sun's coming out. Might dry that old gear out a bit.

thought: heavy-looking, old but holding together
line: Heavy-looking stuff. Old, but it's held together.

thought: wonders if it's an heirloom
line: Is that an heirloom? It's got that look about it.

thought: Horvik's armour never lasts like old gear
line: Horvik's armour never lasts like that old gear has. Shoddy, the lot.

thought: seen better days, like everyone
line: Funny old gear on that one. Seen better days, but who hasn't.

thought: it looks older than she is
line: Good heavens, that gear looks older than I am!

thought: the museum would want it
line: The museum would give its eye teeth for that old gear.

thought: old armour; she'd want to know where it's been
line: Gear that old... I'd want to know where it's been.

thought: it could do with a polish
line: That gear could do with a good polish, if you don't mind me saying.

thought: cold for the season; the old gear looks warmer than her coat
line: Cold for the time of year. That old gear looks warmer than my coat.

thought: heard you can't buy one
line: Can't buy one of those capes for any money, they say.

thought: recognises the cape; you beat TzTok-Jad
line: You saw off TzTok-Jad for that cape? Fair play.

thought: it shifts like a coal fire
line: Looks just like a coal fire, that cape. All shifting about.

thought: tells a friend not to stare, it's earned
line: That's a fire cape, that. Don't stare, it was earned.

thought: she can't sit through a hot bath, never mind a fire cave
line: Can't sit through a hot bath, me, never mind a fire cave.

thought: worn without fuss
line: You wear that cape with no fuss at all. Very proper.

thought: the guards couldn't get one between them
line: The palace guards couldn't get one of those between them.

thought: the colours are like embers in her grate
line: Ooh, the colour on that! Like the embers in my grate.

thought: wonders if it's warm
line: Is it warm, that cape? It looks warm.

thought: cold day; would stand next to it
line: Cold old day. I'd stand by that cape, if you'd let me.

thought: the Herald prints scandal, not fire capes
line: The Herald never mentions the fire capes. Too busy with scandal.

thought: Thessalia sells capes, but not that one
line: Look, a fire cape. Thessalia doesn't stock those, I'll bet.

thought: every wave in that cave; takes nerve
line: Must have taken some nerve, every wave of that cave.

thought: can't be bought, so it's honestly earned
line: Very fine cape. Honestly earned, by the look of it.

thought: shame it gives off no light on dark nights
line: Doesn't even light the street, that cape. Shame, on these dark nights.

thought: keep that cape away from Baraek's furs
line: Keep that cape away from Baraek's furs, would you, guv?

thought: all that flame and no light; a fraud
line: All that flame and not a glimmer of light. Bit of a fraud, that cape.

thought: flash cape for the square; off to see the king
line: Flash cape for the square. Off to see the king, are we?

thought: here comes the bonfire
line: Look out, here comes the bonfire.

thought: fire capes everywhere; the thatchers must be fretting
line: Fire capes everywhere lately. The thatchers must be beside themselves.

thought: take it off before the Blue Moon
line: You'll want that cape off before you go in the Blue Moon.

thought: sat in the fire and the fire won
line: Looks like you sat in the fire and the fire won.

thought: only came out for bread and there's a fire on legs
line: Fire on legs, now. I only came out for bread.

thought: does it come in another colour
line: Does it come in any other colour, or just on fire?

thought: couldn't buy one so sat in a cave
line: Couldn't buy one, so you went and sat in a cave for it?

thought: they think they're a lamp
line: Don't get too close. That one thinks they're a lamp.

thought: warm enough already today
line: Warm enough today without you bringing that cape out.

thought: all those waves and dressed as a hearth rug
line: All those waves, and you've come out dressed as a hearth rug.

thought: can't buy them; saves anyone being blamed
line: They say you can't buy those. Saves anyone being blamed for it.

thought: fire! no, just that cape
line: Fire! Oh. No, it's just that cape again.

thought: black rock and lava on a cape; seen everything now
line: Black rock and lava on a cape. I've seen everything now.

thought: cracked like a dry riverbed with fire in the gaps
line: Cracked like a dry riverbed, that cape, with fire in the gaps.

thought: heard it's the best cape there is
line: Best cape there is, they say. Better than the fire one, even.

thought: that's lava they're wearing
line: That's lava they're wearing. Lava, on a cape.

thought: lava for a cape; she can't carry soup without spilling
line: Lava for a cape. I can't carry soup without spilling it.

thought: warm today; must be roasting
line: Warm one today. You must be roasting under that.

thought: like a cooling pie crust with the filling through
line: Looks like a pie crust cooling, that, with the filling coming through.

thought: it moves on its own
line: Does it ever stop moving, that cape?

thought: heard somebody beat TzKal-Zuk at the bottom of it all
line: Somebody beat TzKal-Zuk for that, they say. Right at the bottom.

thought: first fire capes, now lava; next it'll be soup
line: First fire capes, now lava ones. Next it'll be capes of soup.

thought: stand back; it's alive or near enough
line: Stand back a bit. That cape's alive, or near enough.

thought: a cape of rock must be heavy
line: Must be heavy, a cape of rock. Your shoulders must ache.

thought: keep it out of the rain; lava and puddles
line: Out of the rain with that, I'd think. Lava and puddles don't mix.

thought: a cape of lava; takes all sorts
line: A cape made of lava... well, it takes all sorts.

thought: she'd not have the nerve for the Inferno
line: I'd not have the nerve for that, cape or no cape.

thought: a partyhat; takes her back to Christmas
line: Ooh, a partyhat! Takes me right back to Christmas, that.

thought: somebody pulled a cracker with them, and got one too
line: Somebody pulled a cracker with you, then. Lucky them.

thought: bright colour; did you get to pick
line: Lovely bright colour. Did you get to pick it?

thought: hasn't seen a real partyhat in years
line: Look, a proper partyhat. Not seen one of those in years.

thought: sits nicely, like a little crown
line: That hat sits very nicely. Like a little crown.

thought: never had a cracker herself
line: Never got so much as a cracker, me. Not one Christmas.

thought: heard they only turn up at Christmas
line: Only turn up at Christmas, they say, hats like that.

thought: keep it straight in the wind
line: Keep it on in this wind, mind. It'd be a shame to lose it.

thought: is it Christmas? no, it's the hat
line: Is it Christmas already? Oh, it's just your hat.

thought: the thieves round here would have it off you
line: The thieves round here would have that hat off you. Shameful lot.

thought: brightens up the square
line: Very jolly. Brightens up the square, a hat like that.

thought: a real one, the points and all
line: That's a real partyhat, that. The points and all.

thought: the colour; you'd spot it from the palace
line: Cor, the colour on that hat! You'd spot it from the palace.

thought: looks brand new; kept nicely
line: Looks brand new, that hat. You've kept it nicely.

thought: fit for the king, and more cheerful than his
line: Fit for the king, that hat. More cheerful than his, I'd say.

thought: so bright she can see it with her eyes shut
line: Bright, that hat. I can see it with my eyes shut.

thought: pulled a cracker and never took the hat off
line: Pulled a cracker and kept the hat on ever since, did you?

thought: off to a party this early
line: Off to a party, are we? Bit early in the day for it.

thought: someone's come from a party and not been home
line: Look, someone's come straight from a party and not been home.

thought: hats like that bring out the thieves, and everyone gets robbed
line: Hats like that bring the thieves out. Then it's the rest of us robbed.

thought: looks like a little crown; king of what
line: Looks like a little crown. King of what, exactly?

thought: never has anyone to pull a cracker with
line: Christmas crackers... I never get anyone to pull one with.

thought: the puller picks the colour; did the other end get a better one
line: Did the other end of the cracker get a better colour?

thought: whoever pulled the cracker has a lot to answer for
line: Whoever pulled that cracker with you has a lot to answer for.

thought: don't laugh, it's meant to be a crown
line: Don't laugh. It's probably meant to be a crown.

thought: windy; the hat won't last
line: Windy today. That hat won't stay on long, I'd wager.

thought: very festive; is there cake
line: Very festive. Is there cake, or is it just the hat?

thought: a partyhat on a grown adult in the street
line: A partyhat... on a grown adult... in the street.
